title: Pronunciation Improvement
description: Improve English pronunciation through sound awareness, word stress, sentence rhythm and a practical daily speaking routine.

body_markdown:
## 1. Focus on clarity

The goal of pronunciation practice is to make your speech easy to understand. You do not need to copy a particular accent. Speak clearly, at a comfortable speed, and pronounce important word endings.

## 2. Practise sound pairs

Read each pair slowly and notice the difference:

| Sound focus | Word pairs |
|---|---|
| V and W | vest / west, vine / wine |
| S and SH | sip / ship, see / she |
| short I and long EE | sit / seat, ship / sheep |
| T and TH | tin / thin, tree / three |

Use a reliable dictionary audio recording to hear the target pronunciation, then repeat.

## 3. Word stress

Many English words have one syllable that is stronger than the others. Listen and repeat:

- TA-ble
- DOC-tor
- a-BOUT
- be-GIN
- im-POR-tant

Capital letters here show the syllable to emphasise, not spelling.

## 4. Sentence stress

In a sentence, important words often receive more emphasis:

- I NEED some HELP.
- WHERE is the BUS stop?
- She WORKS in a HOSPITAL.

Do not stress every word equally. Let the sentence sound natural.

## 5. Practise word endings

Say the final sounds clearly:

- work, help, desk, asked, worked
- books, bags, watches

Avoid adding an extra vowel after a final consonant.

## 6. Five-minute daily routine

1. Listen to five words.
2. Repeat each word slowly.
3. Practise the words in sentences.
4. Record your voice.
5. Listen and choose one sound to improve.

## 7. Speaking practice

Read aloud: “I want to improve my English pronunciation. I practise every day. I speak slowly and clearly.” Repeat it twice, focusing on word stress and clear endings.

faq.question: Do I need to speak with a British or American accent?
faq.answer: No. Focus on clear and understandable speech rather than copying a particular accent.

faq.question: How can I practise word stress?
faq.answer: Listen to a reliable pronunciation recording, identify the stronger syllable and repeat the word aloud.

faq.question: How much pronunciation practice is useful?
faq.answer: Five to ten focused minutes each day is a good starting point.
